facts.statement: The genus Knoetschkesuchus was described by Schwarz and colleagues in 2017.
facts.quote: authority: Schwarz et al., 2017

facts.statement: The genus contains two species: the type species K. langenbergensis and K. guimarotae, which was originally classified as Theriosuchus guimarotae.
facts.quote: subdivision: K. langenbergensis Schwarz et al., 2017 (type) K. guimarotae (Schwarz & Salisbury, 2005) (originally Theriosuchus guimarotae)

facts.statement: Knoetschkesuchus is a small atoposaurid crocodylomorph found in the Late Jurassic of Germany and Portugal.
facts.quote: Knoetschkesuchus is a genus of small atoposaurid crocodylomorph from the Late Jurassic of Germany and Portugal.

facts.statement: Knoetschkesuchus primarily fed on small prey such as invertebrates, amphibians, and mammals.
facts.quote: that primarily fed on small prey, including invertebrates, amphibians, and mammals.

facts.statement: Knoetschkesuchus is distinguished from other atoposaurids by having only two distinct types of teeth and lacking leaf-shaped teeth.
facts.quote: Knoetschkesuchus only has two distinct types of teeth, lacking the leaf-shaped teeth seen in other atoposaurids.

facts.statement: The deposits containing K. langenbergensis date to the Upper Kimmeridgian stage of the Jurassic.
facts.quote: These deposits have been dated to the Upper Kimmeridgian stage of the Jurassic

facts.statement: The species K. guimarotae originates from the Guimarota quarry near Leiria, Portugal.
facts.quote: K. guimarotae originates from the lignite layers of the Guimarota quarry, located near Leiria, Portugal.

facts.statement: The Guimarota strata containing K. guimarotae have been dated to the Kimmeridgian based on fossil ostracods.
facts.quote: which has been dated to the Kimmeridgian on the basis of fossil ostracods.

facts.statement: K. guimarotae measures a maximum of 55 cm in length, consistent with other small Atoposauridae.
facts.quote: As with other members of the Atoposauridae, Knoetschkesuchus is very small, with K. guimarotae measuring only 55 cm long at maximum.

facts.statement: Both species of Knoetschkesuchus were quadrupedal with long and slender limbs.
facts.quote: Typical of the group, both species were quadrupedal, bearing long and slender limbs.

facts.statement: Both species have two rows of bony, rectangular osteoderms on their backs that are wider than they are long.
facts.quote: The backs of both of the known species are covered with two rows of bony rectangular osteoderms, centred at the midline, that are wider than they are long.

facts.statement: The skull of Knoetschkesuchus is relatively short, with the snout comprising 47% of skull length in K. langenbergensis and 42% in K. guimarotae.
facts.quote: The skull of Knoetschesuchus is relatively short, with the snout taking up 47% of skull length in K. langenbergensis and 42% in K. guimarotae

facts.statement: The short snouts of Knoetschkesuchus allow them to be classified as brevirostrine crocodilians.
facts.quote: which allows them to be classified as brevirostrine crocodilians.

facts.statement: The antorbital fenestra is small (9% the length of the eye socket) and its presence is unique to Knoetschkesuchus among atoposaurids.
facts.quote: The oval-shaped antorbital fenestra is small, being only 9% the length of the eye socket; its presence is unique to both species of the genus among atoposaurids.

facts.statement: In Knoetschkesuchus, the pterygoid bone on the bottom of the skull is approximately twice as wide as it is long.
facts.quote: On the bottom of the skull, the pterygoid is about twice as wide as it is long.

facts.statement: Unlike Theriosuchus, the choanae in Knoetschkesuchus are not embedded in a wide bowl-like depression.
facts.quote: In Theriosuchus, unlike Knoetschkesuchus, the choanae are embedded in a wider bowl-like depression.

facts.statement: In K. langenbergensis, the convexity found on the bottom of the jaw in K. guimarotae is replaced by a concavity.
facts.quote: The latter convexity is replaced by a concavity in K. langenbergensis.

facts.statement: The oval-shaped external mandibular fenestra is a feature unique to the genus Knoetschkesuchus among atoposaurids.
facts.quote: The presence of the oval-shaped external mandibular fenestra is unique to the genus among atoposaurids.

facts.statement: Both species of Knoetschkesuchus possess only two distinct types of teeth, a trait unique among atoposaurids.
facts.quote: Both species of Knoetschkesuchus have only two distinct types of teeth, uniquely among atoposaurids.

facts.statement: Both species of Knoetschkesuchus have five premaxillary teeth, with the fourth being about one-third larger than the others.
facts.quote: There are 5 premaxillary teeth in both species, the fourth of which is about a third larger relative to the others.

facts.statement: The maxilla of K. langenbergensis has 12 distinct tooth sockets.
facts.quote: The maxilla has 12 distinct sockets in K. langenbergensis.

facts.statement: The dentary of K. langenbergensis exhibits 21 teeth, while K. guimarotae has at least 20.
facts.quote: Meanwhile, the dentary exhibits 21 teeth in K. langenbergensis and at least 20 in K. guimarotae.

facts.statement: Specimens of K. langenbergensis were preliminarily described in a 2006 paper by Hans-Volker Karl et al. and initially referred to the genus Theriosuchus.
facts.quote: When the known specimens of K. langenbergensis were first described in a preliminary fashion by a 2006 paper from Hans-Volker Karl et al., they were referred to the genus Theriosuchus.

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analyses consistently show that Atoposauridae, represented by Knoetschkesuchus, Theriosuchus, and Alligatorium, forms a monophyletic clade.
facts.quote: The phylogenetic trees recovered by this analysis consistently found that Atoposauridae, represented by Knoetschkesuchus, Theriosuchus, and Alligatorium, forms a monophyletic clade.

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analysis strongly supports a close relationship between K. langenbergensis and K. guimarotae, excluding other Theriosuchus species, as evidence for their separation into the genus Knoetschkesuchus.
facts.quote: Within this clade, a close relationship between K. langenbergensis and K. guimarotae, excluding other Theriosuchus species, was strongly supported, providing further evidence of these two species forming a separate genus.

facts.statement: Researchers noted that the nasal bones completely divide the nostrils in Knoetschkesuchus, a trait not seen in the genus Theriosuchus, suggesting a distinction between them.
facts.quote: However, they noted that the nasals essentially completely divide the nostrils to the exclusion of other bones, which is not seen in the genus of Theriosuchus.

facts.statement: Schwarz et al. cited the fact that K. langenbergensis differs in four out of nine traits from the Theriosuchus diagnosis as a basis for separating it into the genus Knoetschkesuchus and revising the diagnosis.
facts.quote: K. langenbergensis differs from this diagnosis in four out of nine traits, which Schwarz et al. cited as a basis for both the generic separation of Knoetschkesuchus and the necessity of revising the diagnosis further.

facts.statement: Knoetschkesuchus was relatively small and likely fed on invertebrates and possibly small vertebrates such as amphibians and mammals.
facts.quote: Being relatively small, Knoetschkesuchus would have mainly fed on invertebrates and possibly small vertebrates (including amphibians and mammals).

facts.statement: During the Kimmeridgian, Europe consisted of scattered archipelagos surrounded by the shallow inland Tethys Ocean.
facts.quote: During the Kimmeridgian, Europe was covered by the shallow inland Tethys Ocean, with exposed landmasses being a series of scattered archipelagos.

facts.statement: The Langenberg Quarry containing K. langenbergensis is part of the Lower Saxony Basin, associated with the Rhenisch, Bohemian, and London-Brabant Massifs.
facts.quote: The Langenberg Quarry, where K. langenbergensis is known from, is part of the Lower Saxony Basin, which would have been part of the landmass associated with the Rhenisch, Bohemian, and London-Brabant Massifs.

facts.statement: Although the Langenberg Quarry environment was shallow marine during the Kimmeridgian, K. langenbergensis was likely not marine as fossils were transported from surrounding islands.
facts.quote: During the Kimmeridgian, it would have been a shallow marine environment; however, this does not imply that K. langenbergensis was marine, since the animals and plants of the Langenberg Quarry were probably transported allochthonously (albeit only by a short distance) from the surrounding islands.

facts.statement: The Guimarota locality where K. guimarotae is found is located in the eastern Lusitanian Basin, part of the Iberian Meseta.
facts.quote: The Guimarota locality is located in the eastern Lusitanian Basin, which is part of the Iberian Meseta.

facts.statement: Two species of Knoetschkesuchus are known: K. langenbergensis described by Schwartz et al. in 2017, and K. guimarotae originally classified as Theriosuchus guimarotae.
facts.quote: Se conocen dos especies: la especie alemana K. langenbergensis, descrita por Schwartz et al. en 2017 con base en dos esqueletos parciales y varios huesos aislados; y la especie portuguesa K. guimarotae, nombrada de tres cráneos parciales así como varios otros elementos, y fue clasificada originalmente como una especie de Theriosuchus.

facts.statement: Specimens of K. langenbergensis include the holotype DFMMh/FV 200, a juvenile skull DFMMh/FV 605, an isolated angular bone DFMMh/FV 261, an isolated left dentary DFMMh/FV 790.12, an isolated femur DFMMh/FV 279, an isolated metatarsal DFMMh/FV 790.11, and a partial skeleton with osteoderms, vertebrae, and ribs DFMMh/FV 325.
facts.quote: Estos incluyen: el espécimen holotipo DFMMh/FV 200, el esqueleto parcial de un adulto con un cráneo; DFMMh/FV 605, el cráneo completo de un juvenil; DFMMh/FV 261, un hueso angular aislado; DFMMh/FV 790.12, un dentario izquierdo aislado; DFMMh/FV 279, un fémur aislado; DFMMh/FV 790.11, metatarso aislado; y DFMMh/FV 325, un esqueleto parcial que incluye osteodermos, vértebras y costillas.

facts.statement: K. langenbergensis specimens were examined using a stereo microscope and described in 2017 by Daniela Schwarz, Maik Raddatz, and Oliver Wings.
facts.quote: Se practicaron exámenes con un estéreo microscopio en los especímenes, los cuales fueron descritos en 2017 en un artículo publicado por Daniela Schwarz, Maik Raddatz y Oliver Wings.

facts.statement: The genus Knoetschkesuchus was established by Schwarz et al. in 2017.
facts.quote: genus_authority: Schwarz et al., 2017

facts.statement: The type species of the genus Knoetschkesuchus is K. langenbergensis.
facts.quote: type_species: Knoetschkesuchus langenbergensis

facts.statement: The species K. guimarotae was originally named Theriosuchus guimarotae by Schwarz & Salisbury in 2005.
facts.quote: subdivision: K. langenbergensis Schwartz et al., 2017 (tipo) K. guimarotae (Schwarz & Salisbury, 2005) (originalmente Theriosuchus guimarotae)

facts.statement: Knoetschkesuchus is an extinct eusuchian atoposaurid crocodyliform that lived during the Late Jurassic in Germany and Portugal.
facts.quote: Knoetschkesuchus es un género de extinto de crocodilomorfo eusuquio atoposáurido que vivió durante el Jurásico Superior en Alemania y Portugal.

facts.statement: Both species of Knoetschkesuchus functioned as small predators ecologically partitioned from other crocodilians, likely originating through dispersal over larger landmasses.
facts.quote: The two species of Knoetschkesuchus were part of similar faunas, in both of which they functioned as small predators ecologically partitioned from the other contemporary crocodilians; it is likely that these faunas originated through dispersal over larger landmasses.

facts.statement: Some researchers previously attributed specimens of K. langenbergensis to another species of Theriosuchus, T. pusillus.
facts.quote: Los especímenes atribuidos a K. langenbergensis también habían sido atribuidos a otra especie de Theriosuchus, T. pusillus por algunos investigadores.

facts.statement: Researchers Schwarz and colleagues assigned the species K. guimarotae to the genus Knoetschkesuchus, though it was originally classified as a species of Theriosuchus.
facts.quote: Schwarz y colaboradores también asignaron una especie adicional a Knoetschkesuchus, K. guimarotae, la cual fue clasificada originalmente como una especie de Theriosuchus.

facts.statement: The species K. guimarotae originates from lignite layers found in the Guimarota quarry near Leiría, Portugal.
facts.quote: K. guimarotae se origina de las capas de lignita de la cantera de Guimarota, localizada cerca de Leiría, Portugal.

facts.statement: The geological formations containing K. guimarotae are dated to the Kimmeridgian stage based on fossil ostracods.
facts.quote: Estas han sido asignadas a la Formación Alcobaça, una subunidad de la Formación Abadia, la cual ha sido datada del Kimmeridgiense con base en sus ostrácodos fósiles.

facts.statement: Fossils of K. guimarotae are housed at the Free University of Berlin's Institute of Geosciences.
facts.quote: Los restos de K. guimarotae están alojados en el Instituto de Ciencias Geológicas de la Universidad Libre de Berlín (de ahí su sigla de IPFUB).

facts.statement: In addition to the type specimen, nearly 400 additional specimens of K. guimarotae are known.
facts.quote: Aparte del espécimen tipo IPFUB Gui Croc 7308 - el cual consiste de un cráneo parcial con mandíbulas, una vértebra del sacro, y dos osteodermos - se conocen cerca de 400 especímenes adicionales

facts.statement: Some specimens show evidence of having been scavenged by other animals.
facts.quote: Algunos de estos muestran marcas de haber sido devorados por carroñeros.

facts.statement: The species K. guimarotae was very small, reaching a maximum length of 55 centimeters.
facts.quote: Como ocurre con otros miembros de Atoposauridae, Knoetschkesuchus era muy pequeño; la especie K. guimarotae solo medía 55 centímetros en su máxima longitud.

facts.statement: The backs of both species are covered with two rows of rectangular bony osteoderms that are wider than they are long.
facts.quote: Los dorsos de ambas especies están cubiertos con dos filas de osteodermos óseos rectangulares, centrados hacia el eje medio, los cuales son más anchos que largos.

facts.statement: Each osteoderm bears a longitudinal keel, though these keels are less developed in K. langenbergensis.
facts.quote: Cada osteodermo lleva una quilla que corre en sentido longitudinal, aunque las quillas están menos desarrolladas en K. langenbergensis.

facts.statement: In K. guimarotae, tail osteoderms had high, sharp keels, were longer than wide near the tail's end, and were domed.
facts.quote: Al menos en K. guimarotae, los osteodermos de la cola tenían quillas altas y afiladas; aquellos cerca de la parte posterior de la cola tendían a ser más largos que anchos, a diferencia de otros osteodermos, y además estaban abovedados.

facts.statement: The vertebrae of K. guimarotae were amphicoelous, meaning they were concave at both ends.
facts.quote: Las vértebras de K. guimarotae eran anficélicas, es decir cóncavas en ambos extremos

facts.statement: The skull of Knoetschkesuchus was relatively short, with the snout comprising 47% of the cranial length in K. langenbergensis and 42% in K. guimarotae.
facts.quote: El cráneo de Knoetschesuchus era relativamente corto, con un hocico que comprendía el 47% de la longitud craneana de K. langenbergensis y el 42% en K. guimarotae.

facts.statement: Two undulations run along the side of the snout, one small on the premaxilla and one larger and wider on the maxilla.
facts.quote: A lo largo del costado del hocico hay dos ondulaciones, una pequeña en el premaxilar y una mayor y más ancha en el maxilar

facts.statement: In K. guimarotae, the upward-facing nostrils are clearly separated by the nasals, whereas this separation is unclear in K. langenbergensis.
facts.quote: Las narinas, que se orientan hacia arriba, están claramente separadas por los nasales en K. guimarotae, pero no es claro que ese sea el caso en K. langenbergensis.

facts.statement: The oval preorbital fenestra is very small, measuring only 9% of the length of the eye orbit.
facts.quote: La fenestra anteorbital en forma de óvalo es muy pequeña, con solo el 9% de la longitud de la órbita ocular

facts.statement: The eye orbit is large and oval, being 54% longer than it is high.
facts.quote: Entretanto, la órbita ocular es grande y ovalada, siendo 54% más larga que alta.

facts.statement: Knoetschkesuchus belongs to the parent group Atoposauridae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Atoposauridae

facts.statement: Knoetschkesuchus is classified in the family Atoposauridae.
facts.quote: Family: Atoposauridae

facts.statement: Knoetschkesuchus is classified in the class Reptilia.
facts.quote: Class: Reptilia

facts.statement: Knoetschkesuchus lived from the Kimmeridgian to the Tithonian stages, between 154.8 and 145.06 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Kimmeridgian to Tithonian (154.8 to 145.06 million years ago)
